references.text: The broader context describing that Moses' face shone after he had spoken with the Lord on Mount Sinai, and that Aaron and the children of Israel were afraid to approach him.
Parallel text explaining Moses' practice of using a veil when speaking to the people, and removing it when he entered into the Lord's presence.

Paulus refers directly to the glory on Moses' face and compares the ministry of the Spirit with the ministry of the letter: εἰ δὲ ἡ διακονία τοῦ θανάτου ἐν γράμμασιν ἐντετυπωμένη λίθοις ἐγενήθη ἐν δόξῃ.
Paulus uses the veil (τὸ κάλυμμα) on Moses' face as a picture of the spiritual blindness that rests over Israel when the Law of Moses is read, but which is removed in Christ.

The contrast between Moses covering his face and believers who with unveiled faces behold the Lord's glory and are transformed: ἡμεῖς δὲ πάντες ἀνακεκαλυμμένῳ προσώπῳ τὴν δόξαν κυρίου κατοπτριζόμενοι.

Paulus continues the theme of God's glory shining in Moses' face, and applies it to the knowledge of God's glory in the face of Jesus Christ: πρὸς φωτισμὸν τῆς γνώσεως τῆς δόξης τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν προσώπῳ Χριστοῦ.
Describes the same event; Exodus 34:29 establishes the cause (the shining skin) while Exodus 34:35 describes the consequence (the veil).
Thematic parallel: The Lord's glory is manifested to the people after Moses has been in God's presence.
Explains the cause of the shining skin: God's 'face-to-face' communication.
